title: Task
description: A developer-sized unit of work, tracing to the component it builds, the requirements it serves and the criteria that accept it, with dependencies and an assigned role. ⚠️ Approved 2026-08-22 after stage 8 was RUN (#144). It closes the trace chain: requirement -> component -> acceptance-criterion -> task -> runbook-step. ⚠️ `role` is a STRING, not a link, and that is a decision rather than an omission — see below.

statement.description: What is to be done, stated so that a recipient could start without asking what was meant. Same field name as every other type's payload (#82).

role.description: Who does it, BY ROLE and never by name (#18). ⚠️ A string rather than a link to a `role-assignment` artifact, and stage 8 is where that was settled: #18 says roles are DISCOVERED from task assignments and there is no roster to maintain, so the set of roles on a project is derived by collecting these values. An artifact holding this string plus an identity would store what a traversal derives — the same refusal as #138's tool signatures, #141's runbook aggregate and #143's roster.

implements.description: The component this task builds. Required and non-empty: a task that implements nothing is the orphan the stage-9 completeness gate looks for.

fulfils.description: The requirements this task serves. Stage 8's `tasks-trace-to-requirement` criterion reads exactly this, which is what makes it mechanical rather than a reading of prose.

acceptedBy.description: The criteria that decide whether this task is done. ⚠️ Not required: a task may legitimately exist before anyone has written how it will be judged, and forcing the link would push people to invent a criterion to satisfy a schema. The lint is the right place to notice the absence.

dependsOn.description: Tasks that must be done first. Ordering is derived from this rather than stored as a sequence number, for the same reason runbook membership is derived from `partOf` (#84): a stored order and a dependency graph disagree the first time anything moves.

tags.description: Changing tags never invalidates an approval (#103).

x-ownsIrreducibleState.owns: A unit of work, who does it, what it builds, and what it waits on. Not derivable: a requirement says what must be true, a component says what implements it, an acceptance criterion says how you would know — none of them says what someone should do next.
traversedBy: #19 role slices — a slice is a query over the task graph, grouped by role
stage 9 completeness gate — a task nothing traces to is an orphan
x-ownsIrreducibleState.deliberatelyNotAType: role. #18 gives it no roster, so it is a task property and the role SET is derived by collecting.

x-unresolvableTraceTargets.description: #75: none. component, requirement, acceptance-criterion and task are all implemented and activated.
